context: Which of the following sequences are A.P ? If it is an A.P, find next two terms.
solution:
In this sequence 5, 12, 19, 26, . . . ,

First term \(= t_1 = 5\), \(t_2 = 12\), \(t_3 = 19\), . . .

\(t_2 - t_1 = 12 - 5 = 7\)

\(t_3 - t_2 = 19 - 12 = 7\)

Here first term is 5 and common difference which is constant is \(d = 7\)

\(\therefore\) This sequence is an A.P.

Next two terms in this A.P. are \(26 + 7 = 33\) and \(33 + 7 = 40\).

Next two terms in given A.P. are 33 and 40

context: Which of the following sequences are A.P ? If it is an A.P, find next two terms.
solution:
In the sequence 2, -2, -6, -10, . . . ,

\(t_1 = 2\), \(t_2 = -2\), \(t_3 = -6\), \(t_4 = -10\) . . .

\(t_2 - t_1 = -2 - 2 = -4\)

\(t_3 - t_2 = -6 - (-2) = -6 + 2 = -4\)

\(t_4 - t_3 = -10 - (-6) = -10 + 6 = -4\)

From this difference between two consecutive terms that is \(t_n - t_{n-1} = -4\)

\(\therefore\) \(d = -4\), which is constant. \(\therefore\) It is an A.P.

Next two terms in this A.P. are \((-10) + (-4) = -14\) and \((-14) + (-4) = -18\)

context: Which of the following sequences are A.P ? If it is an A.P, find next two terms.
solution:
In the sequence 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, . . . ,

In this sequence difference between two consecutive terms is not constant.

\(\therefore\) This sequence is not an A.P.

In the sequence \(\dfrac{3}{2}\), \(\dfrac{1}{2}\), \(-\dfrac{1}{2}\), \(-\dfrac{3}{2}\), . . . ,

\(t_2 - t_1 = \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{3}{2} = -\dfrac{2}{2} = -1\)

\(t_3 - t_2 = -\dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2} = -\dfrac{2}{2} = -1\)

\(t_4 - t_3 = -\dfrac{3}{2} - \left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = -\dfrac{3}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} = -\dfrac{2}{2} = -1\)

Here the common difference \(d = -1\) which is constant.

\(\therefore\) Given sequence is an A.P. Let's find next two terms of this A.P.

\(-\dfrac{3}{2} - 1 = -\dfrac{5}{2}\),   \(-\dfrac{5}{2} - 1 = -\dfrac{7}{2}\)

stem:
Which term of the following A.P. is 560 ?

2, 11, 20, 29, . . .
solution:
Given A.P. 2, 11, 20, 29, . .

Here \(a = 2\), \(d = 11 - 2 = 9\)

\(n^{\text{th}}\) term of this A.P. is 560.

\(t_n = a + (n - 1)d\)

\(\therefore\) \(560 = 2 + (n - 1) \times 9\)

\(= 2 + 9n - 9\)

\(\therefore\) \(9n = 567\)

\(\therefore\) \(n = \dfrac{567}{9} = 63\)

\(\therefore\) \(63^{\text{rd}}\) term of given A.P. is 560.

stem: Check whether 301 is in the sequence 5, 11, 17, 23, . . . ?
solution:
In the sequence 5, 11, 17, 23, . . .

\(t_1 = 5\), \(t_2 = 11\), \(t_3 = 17\), \(t_4 = 23\), . . .

\(t_2 - t_1 = 11 - 5 = 6\)

\(t_3 - t_2 = 17 - 11 = 6\)

\(\therefore\) This sequence is an A.P.

First term \(a = 5\) and \(d = 6\)

If 301 is \(n^{\text{th}}\) term, then.

\(t_n = a + (n - 1)d = 301\)

\(\therefore\) \(301 = 5 + (n - 1) \times 6\)

\(= 5 + 6n - 6\)

\(\therefore\) \(6n = 301 + 1 = 302\)

\(\therefore\) \(n = \dfrac{302}{6}\). But it is not an integer.

\(\therefore\) 301 is not in the given sequence.

stem: The \(10^{\text{th}}\) term and the \(18^{\text{th}}\) term of an A.P. are 25 and 41 respectively then find \(38^{\text{th}}\) term of that A.P., similarly if \(n^{\text{th}}\) term is 99. Find the value of \(n\).
solution:
In the given A.P. \(t_{10} = 25\) and \(t_{18} = 41\).

We know that, \(t_n = a + (n - 1)d\)

\(\therefore\) \(t_{10} = a + (10 - 1)d\)

\(\therefore\) \(25 = a + 9d\) . . . (I)

Similarly \(t_{18} = a + (18 - 1)d\)

\(\therefore\) \(41 = a + 17d\) . . . (II)

\(25 = a + 9d\) . . . From (I) .

\(a = 25 - 9d\)

Substituting this value in equation II.

\(\therefore\) Equation (II) \(a + 17d = 41\)

\(\therefore\) \(25 - 9d + 17d = 41\)

\(8d = 41 - 25 = 16\)

\(d = 2\)

Substituting \(d = 2\) in equation I.

\(a + 9d = 25\)

\(\therefore\) \(a + 9 \times 2 = 25\)

\(\therefore\) \(a + 18 = 25\)   \(\therefore\) \(a = 7\)

Now, \(t_n = a + (n - 1)d\)

\(\therefore\) \(t_{38} = 7 + (38 - 1) \times 2 = 7 + 37 \times 2 = 7 + 74 = 81\)

If \(n^{\text{th}}\) term is 99, then to find value of \(n\).

\(t_n = a + (n - 1)d\)

\(99 = 7 + (n - 1) \times 2\)

\(99 = 7 + 2n - 2\)

\(99 = 5 + 2n\)

\(\therefore\) \(2n = 94\)

\(\therefore\) \(n = 47\)

\(\therefore\) In the given progression \(38^{\text{th}}\) term is 81 and 99 is the \(47^{\text{th}}\) term.

stem: Find the sum of first \(n\) natural numbers.
solution:
First \(n\) natural numbers are 1, 2, 3, . . . , \(n\).

Here \(a = 1\), \(d = 1\), \(n^{\text{th}}\) term \(= n\)

\(\therefore\) \(S_n = 1 + 2 + 3 + \ldots + n\)

\(S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}\)[First term + last term] . . . . . (by the formula)

\(= \dfrac{n}{2}[1 + n]\)

\(= \dfrac{n(n + 1)}{2}\)

\(\therefore\) Sum of first \(n\) natural number is \(\dfrac{n(n + 1)}{2}\).

stem: Find the sum of first \(n\) even natural numbers.
solution:
First \(n\) even natural numbers are 2, 4, 6, 8, . . . , \(2n\).

\(t_1 =\) First term \(= 2\), \(t_n =\) last term \(= 2n\)

**Method I**

\(= \dfrac{n}{2}[t_1 + t_n]\)

\(= \dfrac{n}{2}[2 + 2n]\)

\(= \dfrac{n}{2} \times 2(1 + n)\)

\(= n(1 + n)\)

**Method II**

\(S_n = 2 + 4 + 6 \ldots + 2n\)

\(= 2(1 + 2 + 3 + \ldots + n)\)

\(= \dfrac{2[n(n + 1)]}{2}\)

\(= n(1 + n)\)

**Method III**

\(S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}[2a + (n - 1)d]\)

\(= \dfrac{n}{2}[2 \times 2 + (n - 1)2]\)

\(= \dfrac{n}{2}[4 + 2n - 2]\)

\(= \dfrac{n}{2}[2 + 2n]\)

\(= \dfrac{n}{2} \times 2(1 + n)\)

\(= n(1 + n)\)

\(\therefore\) Sum of first \(n\) even natural numbers is \(n(1 + n)\).

stem: Find the sum of all odd numbers from 1 to 150.
solution:
1 to 150 all odd numbers are 1, 3, 5, 7, . . . , 149.

Which is an A.P.

Here \(a = 1\) and \(d = 2\). First let's find how many odd numbers are there from 1 to 150, so find the value of \(n\), if \(t_n = 149\)

\(t_n = a + (n - 1)d\)

\(149 = 1 + (n - 1)2\)   \(\therefore\) \(149 = 1 + 2n - 2\)

\(\therefore\) \(n = 75\)

Now let's find the sum of these 75 numbers   \(1 + 3 + 5 + \ldots + 149\).

\(a = 1\) and \(d = 2\), \(n = 75\)

**Method I**   \(S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}[2a + (n - 1)d]\)

\(S_n = \dfrac{75}{2}[2 \times 1 + (75 - 1) \times 2]\)

\(S_n = \dfrac{75}{2} \times 150\)

\(S_n = 5625\)

**Method II**   \(S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}[t_1 + t_n]\)

\(S_n = \dfrac{75}{2}[1 + 149]\)

\(S_n = \dfrac{75}{2} \times 150\)

\(S_n = 5625\)

\(\therefore\) The sum of all odd numbers from 1 to 150 is 5625.

stem: A mixer manufacturing company manufactured 600 mixers in \(3^{\text{rd}}\) year and in \(7^{\text{th}}\) year they manufactured 700 mixers. If every year there is same growth in the production of mixers then find (i) Production in the first year (ii) Production in \(10^{\text{th}}\) year (iii) Total production in first seven years.
solution:
Addition in the number of mixers manufactured by the company per year is constant therefore the number of production in successive years is in A.P.

(i) Let's assume that company manufactured \(t_n\) mixers in the \(n^{\text{th}}\) year then as per given information,

\(t_3 = 600\), \(t_7 = 700\)

We know that \(t_n = a + (n - 1)d\)

\(t_3 = a + (3 - 1)d\)

\(a + 2d = 600\) . . . (I)

\(t_7 = a + (7 - 1)d\)

\(t_7 = a + 6d = 700\) . . . (II)

\(a + 2d = 600\)  \(\therefore\) Substituting \(a = 600 - 2d\) in equation (II),

\(600 - 2d + 6d = 700\)

\(4d = 100\)   \(\therefore\) \(d = 25\)

\(a + 2d = 600\)   \(\therefore\) \(a + 2 \times 25 = 600\)

\(a + 50 = 600\)   \(\therefore\) \(a = 550\)

\(\therefore\) Production in first year was 550.

(ii) \(t_n = a + (n - 1)d\)

\(t_{10} = 550 + (10 - 1) \times 25 = 550 + 225\)

Production in \(10^{\text{th}}\) year was 775.

(iii) For finding total production in first 7 years let's use formula for \(S_n\).

\(S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}[2a + (n - 1)d]\)

\(S_n = \dfrac{7}{2}[1100 + 150] = \dfrac{7}{2}[1250] = 7 \times 625 = 4375\)

Total production in first 7 years is 4375 mixers.

stem: Ajay sharma repays the borrowed amount of \(\text{Rs. }3{,}25{,}000\) by paying \(\text{Rs. }30500\) in the first month and then decreases the payment by \(\text{Rs. }1500\) every month. How long will it take to clear his amount ?
solution:
Let the time required to clear the amount be \(n\) months. The monthly payment decreases by \(\text{Rs. }1500\). Therefore the payments are in A.P.

First term \(= a = 30500\), \(d = -1500\)

Amount \(= S_n = 3{,}25{,}000\)

\(S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}[2a + (n - 1)d]\)

\(3{,}25{,}000 = \dfrac{n}{2}[2 \times 30500 + (n - 1)d]\)

\(= \dfrac{n}{2}[2 \times 30500 - 1500n + 1500]\)

\(3{,}25{,}000 = 30500n - 750n^2 + 750n\)

\(\therefore\) \(750n^2 - 31250n + 325000 = 0\)

divide both sides by 250.

\(\therefore\) \(3n^2 - 125n + 1300 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(3n^2 - 60n - 65n + 1300 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(3n(n - 20) - 65(n - 20) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \((n - 20)(3n - 65) = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(n - 20 = 0\), \(3n - 65 = 0\)

\(\therefore\) \(n = 20\) or \(n = \dfrac{65}{3} = 21\dfrac{2}{3}\)

In an A.P. \(n\) is a natural number.

\(\therefore\) \(n \neq \dfrac{65}{3}\)   \(\therefore\) \(n = 20\)

(Or, after 20 months, \(S_{20} = 3{,}25{,}000\) then the total amount will be repaid. It is not required to think about further period of time.)

\(\therefore\) To clear the amount 20 months are needed.

stem: Anvar saves some amount every month. In first three months he saves \(\text{Rs. }200\), \(\text{Rs. }250\) and \(\text{Rs. }300\) respectively. In which month will he save \(\text{Rs. }1000\) ?
solution:
Saving in first month \(\text{Rs. }200\); Saving in second month \(\text{Rs. }250\); .....

200, 250, 300, . . .   this is an A.P.

Here \(a = 200\), \(d = 50\), Let's find \(n\) using \(t_n\) formula and then find \(S_n\).

\(t_n = a + (n - 1)d\)

\(= 200 + (n - 1)50\)

\(= 200 + 50n - 50\)

\(1000 = 150 + 50n\)

\(150 + 50n = 1000\)

\(50n = 1000 - 150\)

\(50n = 850\)

\(\therefore\) \(n = 17\)

In the \(17^{\text{th}}\) month he will save \(\text{Rs. }1000\).

Let's find that in 17 months how much total amount is saved.

\(S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}[2a + (n - 1)d]\)

\(= \dfrac{17}{2}[2 \times 200 + (17 - 1) \times 50]\)

\(= \dfrac{17}{2}[400 + 800]\)

\(= \dfrac{17}{2}[1200]\)

\(= 17 \times 600 = 10200\)

In 17 months total saving is \(\text{Rs. }10200\).

stem:
As shown in the figure, take point A on the line and draw a half circle \(P_1\) of radius 0.5 with A as centre. It intersects given line in point B. Now taking B as centre draw a half circle \(P_2\) of radius 1 cm which is on the other side of the line.

Now again taking A as centre draw a half circle \(P_3\) of radius 1.5 cm. If we draw half circles like this having radius 0.5 cm, 1 cm, 1.5 cm, 2 cm, we get a figure of spiral shape. Find the length of such spiral shaped figure formed by 13 such half circles. \(\left(\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}\right)\)
solution:
Semi circumferences \(P_1\), \(P_2\), \(P_3\), . . . are drawn by taking centres A, B, A, B,... It is given that radius of the first circle is 0.5 cm. The radius of the second circle is 1.0 cm,... From this information we will find \(P_1\), \(P_2\), \(P_3\), . . . \(P_{13}\).

Length of the first semi circumference \(= P_1 = \pi r_1 = \pi \times \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\)

\(P_2 = \pi r_2 = \pi \times 1 = \pi\)

\(P_3 = \pi r_3 = \pi \times 1.5 = \dfrac{3}{2}\pi\)

The lengths are \(P_1\), \(P_2\), \(P_3\), . . ., and the numbers \(\dfrac{1}{2}\pi\), \(1\pi\), \(\dfrac{3}{2}\pi\), . . . are in A.P.

Here \(a = \dfrac{1}{2}\pi\), \(d = \dfrac{1}{2}\pi\), From this let's find \(S_{13}\).

\(S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}[2a + (n - 1)d]\)

\(S_{13} = \dfrac{13}{2}\left[2 \times \dfrac{\pi}{2} + (13 - 1) \times \dfrac{1}{2}\pi\right]\)

\(= \dfrac{13}{2}[\pi + 6\pi]\)

\(= \dfrac{13}{2} \times 7\pi\)

\(= \dfrac{13}{2} \times 7 \times \dfrac{22}{7}\)

\(= 143\) cm.

\(\therefore\) The total length of spiral shape formed by 13 semicircles is 143 cm.

\(\text{Rs. }1000\) is invested at 10 percent simple interest. Check at the end of every year if the total interest amount is in A.P. If this is an A.P. then find interest amount after 20 years. For this complete the following activity.

Simple interest \(= \dfrac{P \times R \times N}{100}\)

Simple interest after 1 year \(= \dfrac{1000 \times 10 \times 1}{100} = \square\)

Simple interest after 2 year \(= \dfrac{1000 \times 10 \times 2}{100} = \square\)

Simple interest after 3 year \(= \dfrac{\square \times \square \times \square}{100} = 300\)

According to this the simple interest for 4, 5, 6 years will be 400, \(\square\), \(\square\) respectively.

From this \(d = \square\), and \(a = \square\)

Amount of simple interest after 20 years

\(t_n = a + (n - 1)d\)

\(t_{20} = \square + (20 - 1)\square\)

\(t_{20} = \square\)

Amount of simple interest after 20 years is \(= \square\)
